title: Tenant-aware live-swap safety net for VPC data plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem:
Redwood Private customers run long-lived sessions and large KV caches in the data plane. Applying runtime upgrades in VPC deployments risks cache loss, session churn, and customer-visible latency spikes. Existing rollout patterns are safe for stateless slices but insufficient when tenants have hot KV state, sticky sessions, or long HTTP/streaming connections.

Goal:
Deliver a repeatable, Terraform-driven upgrade orchestration (SafeSwap) that performs tenant-aware live swaps with transactional KV handoff, session stabilization, and automatic rollback on degraded health — all without application-visible downtime. Must work for both Helm/manifest-based private installs and Terraform-managed VPC modules.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: orchestration workflow, IaC hooks (Terraform + module updates), runtime agent changes to support transactional handoff, synthetic health gating, and automated rollback playbook.
- Out of scope: wholesale changes to customer application session behavior or model storage format. Not changing public API surface.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Preflight (Terraform plan step): run tenant discovery and collect slice metadata (active sessions, KV hotkeys, cache priming score). Produce a traffic-fence plan artifact.
2) Prewarm & prime: deploy new runtime nodes behind isolated routing; run targeted priming for top N hotkeys per-tenant using a priming worker. Verify KV cache hit rates and median tail latency against thresholds.
3) Session-stabilize & handoff: enable a short-lived proxy sidecar that coordinates transactional KV handoff per-tenant. For HTTP/websocket sessions, transfer sticky affinity via a controlled connection quiesce. For streaming RPC, replay last-writer checkpoints.
4) Canary & synthetic gating: shift traffic in tenant-aware increments (configurable per-tenant percentages) and run synthetic probes that simulate observed production prompt/seq-length distribution. Monitor KPIs for 3x the p99 baseline window.
5) Automated rollback and sheltering: if metrics breach thresholds (see acceptance criteria), automatically revert routing to previous nodes, restore KV ownership, and run rollback diagnostics. Produce a rollback-runbook artifact with root-cause hints.
6) Finalize: once stability is observed for an N-minute observation window, reconfigure Terraform state to make the new nodes primary and remove the old nodes.

Terraform / IaC changes required:
- New module outputs and hooks: preflight plan hook, traffic-fence artifact storage (S3), and a phased-apply plan that supports staging variables per-tenant.
- Add lifecycle and depends_on guards to prevent tombstoning primary slices until post-cutover validation completes.
- Provide an option to toggle agent-based handoff vs. external proxy handoff for customer compatibility.

Runtime agent changes:
- Lightweight handoff API to freeze writes for a tenant, snapshot hotkey list, stream snapshot to new node, and ack resume.
- Probe endpoints exposing fine-grained metrics (kv_hit_rate_1m, tenant_active_sessions, handoff_latency_ms).
- Backpressure hooks so the orchestrator can pause cutover when overloaded.

Observability and runbook:
- Dashboards per-tenant showing pre/post-cutover KV hit rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error budget burn, and synthetic probe success rate.
- Automated Incident Runbook: steps for manual rollback, key queries, and common failure causes (network ACL misconfig, CSP rate limits, agent handshake failures).

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
- A staged rollout (non-production cluster) completes without request failures for simulated tenants with steady-state sessions.
- Synthetic probe pass rate >= 99% during canary window; p99 latency delta <= +20% vs baseline.
- Automatic rollback triggers within 2 minutes of breach and completes reversion in <5 minutes for 95% of test cases.
- Terraform plan/apply workflow produces deterministic traffic-fence artifacts and the state reflects new primaries only after validation window.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: incomplete priming leads to cold misses and latency spikes. Mitigation: conservative priming of top-1k hotkeys per-tenant, autoscale priming workers.
- Risk: multi-tenant blast radius if isolation fails. Mitigation: tenant-scoped cutover and safety circuit breakers; strict IAM scoping on IaC hooks.
- Risk: rollback flapping. Mitigation: enforce cooldowns and explainable backoff policy in orchestrator.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module updates (preflight hooks, staged-apply variables) + tests.
- Runtime agent handoff endpoints + integration tests.
- SafeSwap orchestration service (stateless controller) with canary scheduler.
- Dashboards and automated runbook generation.
- End-to-end demo runbook and test checklist for Solutions/SEs.
acceptance_criteria: Can complete a full staged rollout in a non-prod VPC with 10 simulated tenants without user-facing errors
Synthetic probe success >= 99% over 15-minute canary windows
Automated rollback triggers and completes within SLOs (rollback start <2m after breach, revert <5m for 95% cases)
Terraform artifacts (traffic-fence.json) generated and stored in S3 after plan stage
Dashboards show pre/post cutover metrics and runbook links are auto-created
